name: Don't shave: hair-growth encouragement for body

image.caption: Example of testosterone in the body and hair growth 3

lead: In chest-hair-maxxing communities, not shaving means leaving chest, torso and limb hair to reach its natural length so its full density shows, as part of looking more masculine. Some practitioners also say shaving makes hair come back coarser or patchier and that stopping lets the true pattern show.

Reference sources report that shaving does not change the thickness, colour or rate of regrowth of terminal hair; the blunt cut end and lack of sun-lightening can make regrowth look different. Body hair is described in the endocrine literature as dependent on androgens and on how sensitive follicles are to them, so density is set mainly by hormones, genetics and age.

paras: People stop shaving, waxing or trimming the area and let hair grow for months, sometimes alongside other efforts to look more masculine. Hair reaches its natural length and shows what is there.

Not shaving carries no medical risk in itself. Hair that is thin or patchy may stay so, and the topic overlaps with discussion of minoxidil, hormones and transplants for body hair, which carry their own risks.

studies.title: Body hair growth in women: normal or hirsute.

angle.text: Chest-hair-maxxing communities leave body hair untrimmed so it reaches its natural length and shows its full density, a more masculine look. Some also believe shaving thickens regrowth; sources that address this report it does not, and density is mostly androgens and genetics.

lead: 'Don't shave' is a practice in the chest-hair-maxxing corner of looksmaxxing culture: leaving chest, torso and limb hair untrimmed so that it reaches its natural density and length. Proponents treat body hair as a secondary sexual characteristic and want it to be as visible as possible.

Medical literature describes body hair as androgen-dependent: scalp hair grows without androgens, whereas body hair requires them [1]. How much body hair a person has is further shaped by the sensitivity of follicles to androgens, by age and by population differences [1][2]. Shaving is not described in these sources as a factor that alters that capacity.

General reference sources report that shaving does not make terminal hair grow back thicker, coarser or darker, and attribute the impression to the blunt cut tip, to hair being shorter and stiffer, and to the lack of sun-bleaching [3]. No controlled studies of 'not shaving' as an appearance strategy have been found.

paras: The practice consists of not shaving, trimming or waxing the chest and body, and letting hair grow for a period before judging it. Participants in chest-hair threads typically describe it as a first step before trying topical or surgical options.

Before puberty most body hair is fine, pale vellus hair. Rising androgens convert follicles in many regions into producing darker, thicker terminal hair, with chest and abdominal hair increasing in men from late puberty into adulthood [2]. Review literature states that body hair growth depends on androgens, in contrast to scalp hair [1].

Hair patterns vary between individuals and populations. Studies of hirsutism in women, for example, show that the amount of terminal body hair in the general population varies with ethnicity [4][5], and a classic clinical scoring method grades hair growth by body region [6]. Enzyme activity such as 5-alpha-reductase, which converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone, is described as one contributor to androgen action in hair follicles [7][8]. Research on testosterone treatment in trans men documents increased body and facial hair as an effect of androgen exposure [9].

No studies found on abstaining from shaving as a way to increase body hair. The related endocrine research above concerns androgen action and hirsutism scoring rather than grooming behaviour [6][1][4][9].

lore.intro: Chest hair is discussed in appearance forums as part of masculine frame, and not shaving is often listed as the free first step in 'chest hair maxxing' guides. Community accounts are anecdotal.
